purpose: Illustrate the author-stated research architecture underlying the portfolio, with selected public project examples
title: Research architecture behind the portfolio
introduction: Research continues around a loop. Questions wait in a queue; one is selected and scoped; evidence, analysis and challenge repeat; a version is published; its repository, deposit and project records are brought into agreement; monitoring or reuse can lead to a revision or a new question. A study can span several stages. A source catalogue, calculation or release record illustrates one step within it.

operations.title: 1. Question queue
operations.summary: Keep candidate questions with the date and reason they were raised. An entry is a lead, not a commitment. No public queue-entry example is linked here.

operations.title: 2. Selection and scope
operations.summary: Choose a question the available evidence can address; define its unit, population, period and comparison, and select a method suited to the question; check existing work and practical purpose. A contribution, useful replication or synthesis can justify proceeding. Otherwise narrow, reframe or archive.

operations.title: 3. Research and challenge
operations.summary: Collect records, preserve provenance and check reporting periods. Retain missing and conflicting evidence. Analyse with inspectable assumptions and quantities, test sensitivity where appropriate, seek counter-evidence, test alternative explanations, examine source support and revise claims that exceed the evidence. Return to scope when the question needs changing.

operations.title: 4. Publish a version
operations.summary: After the author’s release decision, publish a version with its method, evidence limits and useful reproduction materials. Preserve earlier editions and make corrections inspectable.

examples.text: The versioned bundle includes the paper, structured inputs, source lookup, reproduction commands and a reuse example.
examples.label: Open the versioned release

operations.title: 5. Align records
operations.summary: Check that the public repository, deposit and project-status record identify the same released version. Project-status records are distinct from registers of methodological decisions. No public alignment receipt is linked here; the component below illustrates decision recording only.

examples.text: Decision registers provide a separate method for recording choices and comparing research runs.
examples.label: Inspect the decision-record component
examples.limit: This is a decision-recording component. It is not evidence that a publication, repository and project record were aligned, or that every study ran the full Lifecycle engine.

operations.title: 6. Monitor and reuse
operations.summary: Revisit on stated dates or when new evidence appears; record any actual reuse and its limits. Reuse does not revalidate findings. The example below shows available reuse materials, not proof of a later run.

examples.text: The release includes a reuse example alongside its paper, structured inputs, source lookup and reproduction commands.
examples.label: Open the versioned release
examples.limit: Materials provided for reuse do not establish that a later reuse or monitoring run occurred, or revalidate the findings.

operations.title: 7. Continue or revise
operations.summary: Continue within the active project, publish a corrected or extended version when warranted, or open a new queue entry if the question itself changes.

operations.title: 8. Archive branches
operations.summary: A question or study can pause, stop, be reframed or merge into other work. Retain the recorded decision and any useful materials. An archived item has not necessarily failed novelty. Missing history stays unrecorded.

verification: The shared structure is the author’s description, supported by method documents and selected project records. Each link illustrates a step or supporting component; it does not certify that a study recorded every stage, used the same software or passed every gate. Missing history is left unrecorded. This map does not revalidate findings. Project-specific reproduction and review limits still apply. No workflow-effectiveness or time-saving baseline was run.
disclosure: The author sets research direction, substantive decisions and release approval. AI models and scripts assist research, coding, drafting and checks.
